Morgan (docs): prepping a single "error reference" entry that covers rate limits, timeouts, and context fallbacks. quick question: do we want both JS + Python + curl examples, or keep the page minimal and link to sdk-snippets?
Lee (sdk): include both SDK snippets (JS/Python) inline, curl for quick repro. keep detailed helpers in sdk-snippets repo and link out.
Priya (runtime): runtime emits a programmatic retry hint now: header `X-RW-Retry-In` (seconds) and response metadata `retry_in`. please document reading Retry-After first, then X-RW-Retry-In as our internal hint.
Morgan (docs): noted. also what exactly do we expose for context trimming? i saw a couple variants in code.
Priya (runtime): canonical fields: `context_truncated` (bool) and `truncated_tokens` (int). we drop earliest tokens to fit the window and set those fields. we also add `fallbacked_to` when we transparently switch to a smaller model.
Lee (sdk): SDK surfaces all three in `response.meta` for both JS and Python. i'll add small helpers: one to trim oldest messages until under threshold and one to surface `retry_in` as a sleep hint.
Devin (product): from a UX POV callout the fallback: when `fallbacked_to` is present show a warning and link to the runbook about quality regressions. avoid saying "auto-downgrade" in docs, we prefer "model fallback" language.
Morgan (docs): good, i'll use "model fallback". can we agree on examples? i'll add: curl, PowerShell curl, JS SDK with backoff+jitter, Python requests using Retry-After/X-RW-Retry-In, and a small prompt-trim helper. keep each snippet ~10 lines.
Lee (sdk): here's the minimal JS backoff snippet i'll include (we'll mirror in sdk-snippets tests):
```js
// JS: basic backoff + context_truncated check
async function callGen(req){
  for(let i=0;i<5;i++){
    const res = await client.generate(req);
    if(!res.meta || res.meta.error !== 'TOO_MANY_REQUESTS') return res;
    const wait = Math.pow(2,i)*100 + Math.random()*100;
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, wait));
  }
  throw new Error('retries exhausted');
}
```
Morgan (docs): and python snippet for parsing Retry-After / X-RW-Retry-In?
Lee (sdk): quick python using requests: 
```py
# Python: respect Retry-After then X-RW-Retry-In
import time, requests
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
if r.status_code == 429:
  ra = r.headers.get('Retry-After')
  hint = r.headers.get('X-RW-Retry-In')
  wait = int(ra) if ra else (int(hint) if hint else 1)
  time.sleep(wait)
  # retry once
```
Priya (runtime): add note: synthetic 429s from our test endpoints use X-RW-Retry-In for millisecond precision. real capacity 429s may set Retry-After in seconds.
Devin (product): docs should explicitly say: do not treat 5xx the same as 429; recommend separate handling: 429 -> backoff+retry, 5xx -> circuit-breaker + alert.
